title: Practicing with Language Models Cultivates Human Empathic Communication
extended_summary:
The paper addresses whether large language models can help people learn to communicate empathy more effectively. Prior work suggests LLM-generated empathic responses are often rated highly when blinded, but people value human empathy more than AI-attributed support. The authors therefore ask whether LLMs can be used not to replace human empathy, but to coach humans in expressing empathy through effective conversational moves such as validation, demonstrating understanding, and encouraging elaboration.

The intervention was Lend an Ear, an online role-playing platform where participants held text conversations with LLM partners simulating personal and workplace troubles. In a preregistered randomized experiment, 968 U.S. Prolific participants were assigned to control, short video instruction, personalized AI coaching, or combined video plus AI coaching. Each participant completed three conversations; treatment participants received feedback between conversations. Outcomes were primarily scored using LLM evaluators across six preregistered empathic communication dimensions, with a second human-rating experiment validating whether higher-scored conversations were also preferred by independent raters.

The study population consisted of U.S. adults recruited online, not students or educators in a formal education setting. The intervention context was a brief online training session lasting about 20 minutes, focused on interpersonal communication skill development rather than classroom learning.

The main conclusion is that personalized LLM coaching substantially improved expressed empathic communication relative to control and video-only instruction, especially by increasing validation, understanding, and elaboration while reducing unsolicited advice and dismissive responses. The authors also report a disconnect between felt or self-reported empathy and expressed empathy, suggesting that empathic communication is a learnable performance skill. Human raters tended to prefer conversations that LLM evaluators scored as more empathic, supporting the validity of the measured improvements.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: ChatGPT was used as the underlying GPT-4o model powering the custom Lend an Ear experimental platform, including LLM role-playing conversational partners, an AI communication coach that provided personalized empathic-communication feedback, and LLM-based evaluators.
identified_tools.use_case: Participants practiced empathic communication in three text-based conversations with GPT-4o-powered LLM role-playing partners on the Lend an Ear platform. In the AI coach condition, ChatGPT provided personalized feedback on participants’ conversations using a framework of empathic communication principles; GPT-4o was also used for post-hoc scoring of empathic communication dimensions.

findings.finding_summary: In the preregistered randomized experiment with n=968 participants and 2,904 conversations, personalized feedback from the AI coach produced a 0.98 SD increase, described as a 2.9 point gain, in overall empathic communication performance. Reliable improvement occurred for 21.6% of participants in the AI coach condition and 26.3% in the combined condition, compared with 2.9% in the control condition; reliable decline was 0.4% in the AI coach and combined conditions.
findings.measure: Overall empathy score calculated as the sum of LLM-evaluated prescriptive behavior ratings minus proscriptive behavior ratings
findings.effect_size: 0.98 SD increase; 2.9 point gain on overall empathy score

findings.finding_summary: Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly improved encouraging elaboration relative to control. The reported standardized intervention effect was β=0.648, p<0.001, for the AI coach condition; combined training showed β=0.621, p<0.001, and video instruction showed a smaller effect of β=0.218, p<0.05.
findings.measure: LLM-evaluated encouraging elaboration in empathic communication

findings.finding_summary: Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly improved validating emotions relative to control. The reported standardized intervention effect was β=0.475, p<0.001, for the AI coach condition; combined training showed β=0.613, p<0.001, and video instruction showed β=0.239, p<0.001.
findings.measure: LLM-evaluated validating emotions in empathic communication

findings.finding_summary: Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly improved demonstrating understanding relative to control. The reported standardized intervention effect was β=0.459, p<0.001, for the AI coach condition; combined training showed β=0.573, p<0.001, and video instruction showed β=0.247, p<0.001.
findings.measure: LLM-evaluated demonstrating understanding in empathic communication

findings.finding_summary: Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly reduced unsolicited advice-giving, a proscriptive empathic-communication behavior. The reported standardized intervention effect was β=-0.679, p<0.001, for the AI coach condition; combined training reduced advice-giving more strongly with β=-1.038, p<0.001, while video instruction increased advice-giving with β=0.205, p<0.05.

Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly reduced dismissing emotions, a proscriptive empathic-communication behavior. The reported standardized intervention effect was β=-0.451, p<0.001, for the AI coach condition; combined training showed β=-0.656, p<0.001, and video instruction showed β=-0.325, p<0.001.
findings.measure: LLM-evaluated dismissing emotions in empathic communication

findings.finding_summary: Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly reduced self-oriented responses, a proscriptive empathic-communication behavior. The reported standardized intervention effect was β=-0.213, p<0.05, for the AI coach condition; the paper reports that combined training reduced advice-giving and dismissing emotions but does not report a significant combined-training effect for self-oriented responses in the excerpt.
findings.measure: LLM-evaluated self-oriented responses in empathic communication

findings.finding_summary: In a second preregistered experiment, n=150 Prolific participants made forced-choice judgments over 150 conversations sampled from the Lend an Ear dataset. Human raters increasingly selected the conversation with the higher LLM empathy score as the score gap widened; logistic regression showed β=0.144, p<.001, OR=1.155, 95% CI [1.12, 1.19], and Bradley-Terry human-preference rankings correlated with LLM scores at Spearman ρ=0.75 and with LLM Elo ratings at ρ=0.85, p<0.001 for both.
findings.measure: Human forced-choice preference for more empathic conversations compared with LLM empathy scores and LLM-derived Elo ratings
findings.effect_size: OR=1.155 per point; Spearman ρ=0.75 with LLM empathy scores; Spearman ρ=0.85 with Elo ratings

quality_tier_rationale: The study used a preregistered randomized experiment with n=968 participants, randomized assignment to control, video, AI coach, and combined conditions, and clustered standard errors. Quality is downgraded from blue because outcomes were primarily short-term, simulated role-play outcomes scored by LLM evaluators, although a second human-rater experiment supported the validity of the scoring.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects of the AI coaching intervention were medium to large, including an overall empathic communication gain of 0.98 SD and subcomponent effects such as β=0.648 for encouraging elaboration and β=-0.679 for reducing advice-giving. Effects were positive for the targeted social-emotional communication skills.
